topics.title: An emitted kilogram is not a human dose
topics.insight: A facility-reported mass tells you a quantity released, not what any person inhaled, swallowed or absorbed.
topics.boundary: Reported quantities require fate, transport, concentration, exposure-route and toxicity evidence before inferring health risk.
topics.next_question: Which chemical, release medium and exposure point could connect this inventory to an actual dose?

topics.title: Corporate production attribution is not a facility map
topics.insight: Carbon Majors attributes production-linked greenhouse gases to fossil-fuel and cement producers, including the combustion of sold products outside their home jurisdictions.
topics.boundary: That methodology does not locate every emission at the producer's headquarters or establish a locally measured toxic release.
topics.next_question: Does the figure include downstream combustion, and where did the physical activity occur?

topics.title: National inventories and producer totals are different ledgers
topics.insight: A territory-based country inventory assigns emissions to places; Carbon Majors assigns production-linked activity to producer entities.
topics.boundary: Adding, ranking or dividing these figures as if they share the same denominator creates misleading comparisons.
topics.next_question: Do the two datasets use the same year, gases, spatial boundary and scope?

topics.title: A number without its unit and year is not a finding
topics.insight: Environmental sources can report annual tonnes released, concentrations, global CO₂-equivalents or historical totals. Each answers a different question.
topics.boundary: An annual mass cannot be compared directly with a concentration, and a historical estimate is not a live condition.
topics.next_question: Can the unit, time interval, geographic boundary and version be written beside every figure?

topics.title: Measured and modeled exposure are different evidence
topics.insight: Exposure assessments may rely on direct monitoring, indirect estimation or reconstruction, depending on data and study design.
topics.boundary: A modeled estimate is not a personal measurement; a single sensor may not represent other times or locations.
topics.next_question: What was measured directly, what was inferred, and what uncertainties accompany both?

topics.title: A screening flag is a reason to investigate
topics.insight: Screening and refined exposure assessments serve different purposes. A preliminary indicator can help decide what requires a closer look.
topics.boundary: A screening-level result is not, by itself, a demonstrated injury, causal link or legal conclusion.
topics.next_question: What evidence and quality controls would a refined assessment need?

topics.title: The five links of an exposure pathway
topics.insight: ATSDR evaluates contaminant source, environmental fate and transport, exposure point, exposure route, and potentially exposed population.
topics.boundary: Knowing an industrial source exists does not establish that contamination reached anyone.
topics.next_question: Which of the five links is directly documented, and which remains unknown?

topics.title: Potential and completed pathways are not synonyms
topics.insight: ATSDR distinguishes potential pathways, where one or more elements remain uncertain, from completed pathways, where all five elements are present.
topics.boundary: Potential is not proof of contact; completed contact is not proof that injury followed.
topics.next_question: What evidence establishes the pathway at the relevant place and time?

topics.title: Even completed exposure does not establish harm
topics.insight: A completed ATSDR pathway describes an exposure opportunity or contact; further scientific evaluation considers dose, toxicity, duration and health effects.
topics.boundary: A pathway classification cannot be converted directly into numbers of illnesses or assigned blame.
topics.next_question: What independent exposure and effect evidence would be needed next?

topics.title: Groundwater can move dissolved contamination
topics.insight: USGS explains that natural and human-generated substances can enter groundwater as water moves through soil and rock; transport depends on site conditions.
topics.boundary: A nearby industrial operation alone does not establish that contamination reached a particular well.
topics.next_question: What do local flow direction, well depth, sampling dates and analytes show?

topics.title: Clear-looking groundwater is not proof of safe chemistry
topics.insight: Groundwater can appear clear while containing dissolved natural or human-generated constituents.
topics.boundary: Appearance cannot substitute for properly collected samples and laboratory analysis of relevant contaminants.
topics.next_question: Is this a private well or public system, and which substances were actually tested?

topics.title: Mercury can concentrate up aquatic food webs
topics.insight: NOAA describes conversion of mercury to methylmercury and its accumulation and magnification through feeding relationships.
topics.boundary: A fish species name alone does not establish a particular meal's concentration or a specific source of pollution.
topics.next_question: What species, location, advisory and contaminant-testing evidence apply?

topics.title: Hazard is not the same as risk
topics.insight: Hazard identification asks whether a substance can cause an adverse effect. Risk characterization also needs relevant dose-response and exposure evidence.
topics.boundary: The fact that a chemical can be toxic does not quantify an individual's risk at an unspecified dose.
topics.next_question: Which exposure conditions make the hazard relevant to this population?

topics.title: Four parts of a defensible health-risk assessment
topics.insight: EPA describes hazard identification, dose-response assessment, exposure assessment and risk characterization as distinct components.
topics.boundary: Skipping steps can turn a plausible concern into an unsupported numerical claim.
topics.next_question: Which component has measured evidence and which still rests on assumptions?

topics.title: Dose depends on more than one reading
topics.insight: Exposure assessment considers magnitude, frequency, duration, route and the exposed population, along with data quality and uncertainty.
topics.boundary: A single point reading cannot establish a lifetime exposure or diagnose a particular health outcome.
topics.next_question: What time series, duration, location and exposure-route evidence are available?

topics.title: The vulnerable life stage can change the analysis
topics.insight: EPA's lead risk research considers how exposure and adverse outcomes can differ across critical life stages and how risk management may reduce harm.
topics.boundary: A community-average value cannot describe a particular child's exposure or medical condition.
topics.next_question: Which population, medium, sampling method and life stage does the evidence actually cover?

topics.title: PFAS is a family, not a single test result
topics.insight: NIH reviews different health associations for PFAS exposures; individual compounds, exposure routes and scientific evidence can differ.
topics.boundary: A label that says only 'PFAS' is insufficient for a compound-specific risk or source attribution.
topics.next_question: Which named PFAS, units, method, detection limits and reporting date were used?

topics.title: Radon risk depends on the building and measurement
topics.insight: EPA provides guidance on testing indoor radon and reducing elevated levels; a building-specific result is needed to understand its conditions.
topics.boundary: County maps or a neighbor's result cannot establish one room's radon concentration.
topics.next_question: Was a suitable indoor test performed, and how long did it sample?

topics.title: A daily air index is not an annual exposure profile
topics.insight: AirNow provides current and forecast air-quality information; WHO's city database describes historical annual concentrations where available.
topics.boundary: Today's AQI and a historical city annual mean answer different questions and cannot describe individual dose alone.
topics.next_question: What monitoring site, averaging period, pollutant and date are being compared?

topics.title: A supplier report does not measure every household tap
topics.insight: EPA's Consumer Confidence Reports describe public water system information and reported quality; local plumbing and private wells can require distinct assessment.
topics.boundary: A system-wide report is not a certified measurement from a particular kitchen faucet or private well.
topics.next_question: Who supplies the water and where would a valid point-of-use sample be collected?

topics.title: A reporting inventory leaves things out
topics.insight: EPA notes that TRI reporting covers specified chemicals and facilities under reporting requirements, not every source of exposure.
topics.boundary: No entry in the inventory does not prove that an area is pollution-free or that a facility has no emissions.
topics.next_question: Was this facility or activity within reporting scope for the substance and year?

topics.title: An enforcement record needs its procedural status
topics.insight: EPA ECHO provides inspections, permits, compliance and enforcement records that researchers can use to investigate facilities.
topics.boundary: An alleged or recorded violation must not automatically be described as a final adjudication or a personal health outcome.
topics.next_question: What agency action, date, facility identifier and final disposition are documented?

topics.title: Money paid, promised and capped are not interchangeable
topics.insight: Publicly reported remedies can include completed payments, future schedules, settlement obligations and maximum caps. POISONERS separates these in its evidence ledger.
topics.boundary: Adding overlapping amounts, changing currencies without method or treating a promise as money already paid misstates the record.
topics.next_question: Which legal instrument, date, original currency and paid-status disclosure supports the amount?

topics.title: A public record is not a liability finding
topics.insight: An emissions inventory, monitoring result and enforcement entry are different classes of evidence and do not by themselves answer every legal causation question.
topics.boundary: Do not infer wrongdoing, fault or individual culpability solely from appearance in a dataset or job title.
topics.next_question: Which jurisdiction, legally established elements and adjudicated findings are actually documented?
